Consistency: no prior public statements on record that conflict with D endorsement.

Best next move: Publicly endorse D and lock consensus. Use “essentially preserved / not significantly altered for the SHM high-affinity read-out” language consistent with bloc, avoid re-introducing B or C, avoid over-absolute normal claims.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The read-out is high-affinity, SHM-bearing, OVA-specific IgG made by a T-dependent germinal centre reaction to repeatedly given s.c. OVA + CpG in BALB/c. In BALB/c the immunodominant epitope OVA323-339 is I-Ad restricted, so the compartment non-redundantly requires AID-dependent deamination in GC B cells, CD40-CD40L Tfh licensing for GC entry/AID up-regulation/selection, and cognate peptide-MHC II presentation of OVA323-339 by I-Ad to OVA-specific CD4+ T cells.

G1 AID-(V18R). V18R is nuclear localisation / catalytic loss-of-function AID. No AID-mediated cytidine deamination in V regions → no SHM, no affinity maturation. High-affinity SHM OVA titre is lost. Unanimous.

G2 CD40-KO. CD40 signalling on B cells from Tfh is obligate for T-dependent GC formation, B cell proliferation, AID induction and selection. Loss essentially abolishes OVA-specific GC and AID-mediated affinity maturation. Unanimous.

G3 H2-IAd-(E137A/V142A). E137/V142 line the I-Aβ1 peptide-binding groove/P1 pocket for OVA323-339. Double alanine abrogates loading/stable presentation of OVA to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. No peptide-MHC II → no OVA-specific Tfh help, no OVA-specific GC, no SHM-derived high-affinity OVA Ig. Unanimous.

G4 CD8-(V247D). V247D impairs CD8/MHC I co-receptor function. Humoral T-dependent affinity maturation to a protein antigen is CD4+/MHC II driven; MHC I/CD8 dispensable for GC SHM. Expected wild-type for high-affinity SHM OVA titre. Unanimous.

G5 H2-IAd-(T139A). Current group consensus: T139 sits in the I-Aβ1 groove platform and makes backbone H-bond contacts that stabilise the OVA323-339–I-Ad complex and support productive TCR engagement. T139A destabilises the peptide-MHC complex, reduces surface presentation of OVA–I-Ad and markedly impairs priming of OVA-specific CD4+ T cells/Tfh and the cognate T-B synapse in GC. For the BALB/c OVA system this is a functional peptide presentation/stability defect, not merely a CD4 co-receptor contact change, and it phenocopies E137A/V142A for the OVA-specific response, leading to loss of the SHM-derived high-affinity OVA compartment. Earlier split about quantitative CD4 contact compensation vs presentation defect is now resolved in favour of a presentation/stability defect.

G6 MyD88-KO. CpG signals via TLR9–MyD88 as adjuvant, augmenting innate DC maturation and magnitude/kinetics of Tfh/GC. With repeated subcutaneous OVA over a month, sustained antigen-driven CD4 T cell help is sufficient to mount a conventional T-dependent GC and AID-mediated SHM programme in the absence of TLR9 signalling. Loss affects magnitude/kinetics, not qualitative abolition of the SHM/high-affinity compartment. Earlier disagreement where some colleagues scored MyD88 loss as a significant qualitative reduction is now rejected; consensus is G6 is essentially wild-type for the qualitative SHM endpoint.

Synthesis converged: Significantly altered high-affinity SHM OVA titre vs WT in G1, G2, G3 and G5. G4 and G6 are expected wild-type for this qualitative SHM read-out. This is option D: G1, G2, G3, G5.

Remaining nuance to keep: mechanistic classification of T139A as peptide-stability/presentation vs CD4 contact, and the quantitative vs qualitative interpretation of MyD88 loss under repeated immunisation. No further unresolved questions for the present choice.

reflection_text.5:
The read-out is high-affinity, SHM-bearing, OVA-specific IgG made by a T-dependent germinal centre reaction to repeatedly given s.c. OVA + CpG in BALB/c. In BALB/c the immunodominant epitope OVA323-339 is I-Ad restricted, so the compartment non-redundantly requires AID-dependent deamination in GC B cells, CD40-CD40L Tfh licensing for GC entry/AID up-regulation/selection, and cognate peptide-MHC II presentation of OVA323-339 by I-Ad to OVA-specific CD4+ T cells.

G1 AID-(V18R). V18R is nuclear localisation / catalytic loss-of-function AID. No AID-mediated cytidine deamination in V regions → no SHM, no affinity maturation. High-affinity SHM OVA titre is lost. Unanimous.

G2 CD40-KO. CD40 signalling on B cells from Tfh is obligate for T-dependent GC formation, B cell proliferation, AID induction and selection. Loss essentially abolishes OVA-specific GC and AID-mediated affinity maturation. Unanimous.

G3 H2-IAd-(E137A/V142A). E137/V142 line the I-Aβ1 peptide-binding groove/P1 pocket for OVA323-339. Double alanine abrogates loading/stable presentation of OVA to I-Ad-restricted CD4+ T cells. No peptide-MHC II → no OVA-specific Tfh help, no OVA-specific GC, no SHM-derived high-affinity OVA Ig. Unanimous.

G4 CD8-(V247D). V247D impairs CD8/MHC I co-receptor function. Humoral T-dependent affinity maturation to a protein antigen is CD4+/MHC II driven; MHC I/CD8 dispensable for GC SHM. Expected wild-type for high-affinity SHM OVA titre. Unanimous.

G5 H2-IAd-(T139A). Current group consensus: T139 sits in the I-Aβ1 groove platform and makes backbone H-bond contacts that stabilise the OVA323-339–I-Ad complex and support productive TCR engagement. T139A destabilises the peptide-MHC complex, reduces surface presentation of OVA–I-Ad and markedly impairs priming of OVA-specific CD4+ T cells/Tfh and the cognate T-B synapse in GC. For the BALB/c OVA system this is a functional peptide presentation/stability defect, not merely a CD4 co-receptor contact change, and it phenocopies E137A/V142A for the OVA-specific response, leading to loss of the SHM-derived high-affinity OVA compartment. Earlier split about quantitative CD4 contact compensation vs presentation defect is now resolved in favour of a presentation/stability defect.

G6 MyD88-KO. CpG signals via TLR9–MyD88 as adjuvant, augmenting innate DC maturation and magnitude/kinetics of Tfh/GC. With repeated subcutaneous OVA over a month, sustained antigen-driven CD4 T cell help is sufficient to mount a conventional T-dependent GC and AID-mediated SHM programme in the absence of TLR9 signalling. Loss affects magnitude/kinetics, not qualitative abolition of the SHM/high-affinity compartment. Earlier disagreement where some colleagues scored MyD88 loss as a significant qualitative reduction is now rejected; consensus is G6 is essentially wild-type for the qualitative SHM endpoint.

Synthesis converged: Significantly altered high-affinity SHM OVA titre vs WT in G1, G2, G3 and G5. G4 and G6 are expected wild-type for this qualitative SHM read-out. This is option D: G1, G2, G3, G5.

Remaining nuance to keep: mechanistic classification of T139A as peptide-stability/presentation vs CD4 contact, and the quantitative vs qualitative interpretation of MyD88 loss under repeated immunisation. No further unresolved questions for the present choice.

reflection_text.2:
The read-out is high-affinity, SHM-bearing, T-dependent IgG to protein antigen OVA after repeated subcutaneous OVA+CpG immunisation in BALB/c. Non-redundant qualitative requirements for the SHM/affinity maturation compartment are AID-dependent deamination in GC B cells, CD40-CD40L Tfh licensing for GC entry/AID up-regulation/selection, and peptide-MHC II presentation of the BALB/c immunodominant OVA323-339 epitope by I-Ad to OVA-specific CD4+ T cells.

G1 AID-(V18R): V18R is nuclear localisation/catalytic loss-of-function AID. No AID-mediated deamination → no SHM-driven affinity maturation. Defect expected. Uncontested.

G2 CD40-KO: CD40 signalling on B cells from Tfh is obligatory for GC formation, proliferation, AID induction and affinity selection. Loss abrogates T-dependent GC and SHM-driven high-affinity OVA Ig. Defect expected. Uncontested.

G3 H2-IAd-(E137A/V142A): E137/V142 line the I-Aβ1 peptide-binding groove/P1 pocket. Double alanine abrogates loading/presentation of OVA323-339 to I-Ad. No peptide-MHC II for OVA-specific CD4+ T cells → no Tfh help, no OVA-specific GC, no SHM high-affinity OVA Ig. Defect expected. Uncontested.

G4 CD8-(V247D): CD8 co-receptor/MHC I defect. Humoral T-dependent affinity maturation to protein antigen is CD4+/MHC II driven. MHC I/CD8 dispensable for GC SHM and high-affinity OVA Ig. No change expected. Uncontested.

G5 H2-IAd-(T139A): T139 sits in the I-Aβ1 groove platform and makes backbone H-bond contacts that stabilise the OVA323-339–I-Ad complex and support productive TCR engagement. T139A destabilises the peptide-MHC complex, reduces surface presentation and impairs priming of OVA-specific CD4+/Tfh cells and GC selection. In the BALB/c OVA system this is functionally a peptide presentation/stability defect and phenocopies E137A/V142A for the OVA-specific response → significant loss of high-affinity SHM OVA titre. Earlier split between CD4 co-receptor contact vs peptide-binding defect is now resolved toward functional presentation loss under repeated high antigen/adjuvant immunisation. Colleagues 1-4,6 now treat as loss; colleague 5 revised from earlier CD4-binding-only view to loss. Consensus for loss holds.

G6 MyD88-KO: CpG signals via TLR9-MyD88 as adjuvant. MyD88 loss blunts innate activation/DC maturation and response magnitude/kinetics, but a conventional T-dependent germinal centre and AID-mediated SHM can be mounted by repeated antigen-driven CD4 T cell help alone. After repeated subcutaneous OVA over a month the qualitative generation of a high-affinity SHM-bearing OVA Ig compartment is preserved. Effect is quantitative magnitude, not qualitative loss of SHM-driven affinity maturation. Colleagues who previously scored G6 as defective have revised to exclude it.

On balance essential non-redundant requirements for high-affinity SHM OVA antibody are AID, CD40 and functional I-Ad presentation of OVA to CD4+ T cells. Significantly different from WT: G1, G2, G3, G5. G4 CD8-V247D and G6 MyD88-KO expected to retain qualitatively normal T-dependent GC/SHM programme under repeated immunisation.

This corresponds to option D: G1, G2, G3, G5.

Remaining nuance: precise structural role of T139A in peptide binding vs CD4 binding and whether MyD88 loss could be scored as “significantly different” on magnitude grounds, but for the qualitative SHM high-affinity titre the group has converged on D.
